long_biography.plain_text:
A procurement problem at General Dynamics gave Paul Andrews the organising idea for TTI: manufacturers needed reliable access to inexpensive electronic parts that larger distributors handled poorly. He built the company around deep stocks of passive, interconnect and electromechanical components, then introduced computerised inventory controls and centralised warehousing as customers became national.

Andrews favoured organic growth, but the purchase of Mouser Electronics added a distinct catalogue-distribution operation. Concerned that a conventional buyer might dismantle the culture he had built, he chose Berkshire Hathaway as TTI's permanent owner. The sale preserved local management, and Andrews continued as chairman and chief executive until his death.

The display name is retained because it is a valid public form; Eugene is proposed in the researchable middle_names field, while the optional suffix field is left unchanged rather than treating the shorter display as erroneous.

The exact date remains in the research record, but the three death-date fields were inventoried as inapplicable under the stale Alive status and are not proposed in this terminal dossier; only mortality_status is corrected.

Andrews learned work and business habits beside his father in a custom-cabinetry company, and Judy Andrews helped him launch TTI with $300. Those are documented ordinary mentoring and spousal support, not evidence of inherited wealth, a transferred electronics business or substantial family-financed takeover capital. Self-made — independent start therefore clears the threshold; Self-made — advantaged start is the strongest considered alternative if material family resources are later documented.

Andrews sold TTI to Berkshire Hathaway in 2007 but continued as chairman and chief executive until death. Founder and Operator are accurate historical relationships, not current ones. Wealth relationship is therefore Unknown after his death, while Technology is used only as the authorised origin-sector fallback because no complete later personal portfolio is available.
